description: Household internet at home: usage, quality and the ER605 router. The ER605 is read over SNMPv3 every 30 s by roles/er605_snmp on ubuntu-dev (an snmp_exporter plus a poller, which keeps an hourly usage ledger and logs reconnects and reboots); availability and latency come from the internet-probe poller on rpi5, which sits behind the ER605.

panels.description: Source: internet_probe_* with site="home", from the internet-probe poller on rpi5, which sits behind the ER605 only. 1 means no probe round failed in the last 15 s; 0 means at least one round reached no tcp or dns target. A blip between two scrapes still shows for a while.
panels.title: Internet now

panels.description: Source: internet_probe_* with site="home", from the internet-probe poller on rpi5, which sits behind the ER605 only. 1 - confirmed downtime / range length (2 failed rounds in a row, about 10 s; blips are not counted). The whole range is the denominator even if the poller started part way in. The Prometheus variable picks the tier: the central one keeps 7 days, the network one 90 days; the Outages row has 30.
panels.title: Availability over the range

panels.description: Source: er605_* from the er605-poll container (roles/er605_snmp), which reads the ER605 over SNMPv3 every 30 s. The ER605 writes offloaded traffic into these counters in batches, tens of seconds late, so rates use a 5 minute window. Totals are exact.
panels.title: WAN download now

panels.description: Source: er605_* from the er605-poll container (roles/er605_snmp), which reads the ER605 over SNMPv3 every 30 s. The ER605 writes offloaded traffic into these counters in batches, tens of seconds late, so rates use a 5 minute window. Totals are exact.
panels.title: WAN upload now

panels.description: Source: er605_* from the er605-poll container (roles/er605_snmp), which reads the ER605 over SNMPv3 every 30 s. Whole household (everything behind the ER605, the homelab included), WAN port eth1, increase over the selected time range. Counters restart on a PPPoE reconnect or a router reboot; increase() adds across those restarts.
panels.title: Downloaded in range

panels.description: Source: er605_* from the er605-poll container (roles/er605_snmp), which reads the ER605 over SNMPv3 every 30 s. Whole household, WAN port eth1, increase over the selected time range.
panels.title: Uploaded in range

panels.description: Source: er605_* from the er605-poll container (roles/er605_snmp), which reads the ER605 over SNMPv3 every 30 s. How long the current PPPoE session to the ISP has been up (sysUpTime minus the last change of pe-wan1_poe). It restarts from zero when the ISP drops the session; the Quality row has the timeline.
panels.title: PPPoE session age

panels.description: Source: er605_* from the er605-poll container (roles/er605_snmp), which reads the ER605 over SNMPv3 every 30 s. How many times the PPPoE session was re-established in the selected range. The count comes from the poller's ledger, so it survives restarts. Older reconnects: --report reconnects on ubuntu-dev.
panels.title: PPPoE reconnects in range

panels.description: Source: er605_* from the er605-poll container (roles/er605_snmp), which reads the ER605 over SNMPv3 every 30 s. Time since the ER605 last booted. Every counter on it restarts from zero then; the usage panels account for that.
panels.title: Router uptime

panels.description: Seconds since the er605-poll container on ubuntu-dev last read the router. Over about 120 means it stopped, or the router did not answer SNMP. The poll status is er605_poll_success.
panels.title: Poller last read

panels.description: Source: er605_* from the er605-poll container (roles/er605_snmp), which reads the ER605 over SNMPv3 every 30 s. The ER605 writes offloaded traffic into these counters in batches, tens of seconds late, so rates use a 5 minute window. Totals are exact.
panels.title: Household WAN throughput (ER605 WAN1, eth1)

panels.description: Source: er605_* from the er605-poll container (roles/er605_snmp), which reads the ER605 over SNMPv3 every 30 s. Increase of the WAN counters per hour, download plus upload stacked. The Prometheus variable picks the tier: the central one keeps 7 days, the network one 90 days; the History row has the ledger for 30.
panels.title: Hourly volume

panels.description: Bytes per day (UTC days) from the WAN counters. The Prometheus variable picks the tier: the central one keeps 7 days, the network one 90 days; the ledger (usage.db on ubuntu-dev, --report day) keeps everything and the next panel shows 30 days from Loki.
panels.title: Daily volume

panels.description: Source: the poller's hourly `usage` lines in Loki (30 days), summed per day; set the time picker to 30 days. Hours are UTC hours, so a day is a UTC day. Each hour's line is written when the hour closes, so the last hour is missing until then. Older: --report day on ubuntu-dev.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time({host="ubuntu-dev", job="docker", container="er605-poll"} |~ "^usage " | logfmt | unwrap download_bytes [1d]))
sum(sum_over_time({host="ubuntu-dev", job="docker", container="er605-poll"} |~ "^usage " | logfmt | unwrap upload_bytes [1d]))

panels.title: Daily volume, 30 days (ledger)

panels.description: Household total from the ER605 WAN counter. The Prometheus variable picks the tier: the central one keeps 7 days, the network one 90 days.
panels.title: Downloaded, last 24 h

panels.description: Household total from the ER605 WAN counter. The Prometheus variable picks the tier: the central one keeps 7 days, the network one 90 days.
panels.title: Uploaded, last 24 h

panels.description: p95 of the 1-minute rate over the selected range (a subquery at 1 minute steps over rate(...[1m])). The ER605 syncs its counters late, so single minutes can read low or high; the p95 and peak are the useful figures, not the single minutes.
panels.title: Download p95 (1-minute rate)

panels.description: p95 of the 1-minute rate over the selected range (a subquery at 1 minute steps over rate(...[1m])). The ER605 syncs its counters late, so single minutes can read low or high; the p95 and peak are the useful figures, not the single minutes.
panels.title: Upload p95 (1-minute rate)

panels.description: Highest 1-minute rate in the selected range (max_over_time over a 1-minute rate subquery). Counter sync lag can bunch traffic into one minute, so a single peak can read high; the p95 is the steadier figure.
panels.title: Download peak (1-minute rate)

panels.description: Highest 1-minute rate in the selected range (max_over_time over a 1-minute rate subquery). Counter sync lag can bunch traffic into one minute, so a single peak can read high; the p95 is the steadier figure.
panels.title: Upload peak (1-minute rate)

panels.description: t7920's nic1 also carries LAN-local traffic, so it can exceed the WAN line briefly.
panels.title: Household vs t7920, download

panels.description: t7920's nic1 also carries LAN-local traffic, so it can exceed the WAN line briefly.
panels.title: Household vs t7920, upload

panels.description: Source: opnsense_interfaces_received_bytes_total and transmitted on the OPNsense WAN interface (homelab) against er605_if_octets_total on the ER605 WAN port (household, homelab included), download plus upload. CAVEAT: OPNsense WAN also carries traffic between the home LAN and the homelab (for example Plex to a Mac at home), so the OPNsense figure is an upper bound on the homelab's internet use, and ER605 WAN minus OPNsense WAN is NOT the rest of the household's share.
panels.title: Homelab (OPNsense WAN) vs household (ER605 WAN)

panels.description: Source: OPNsense WAN bytes (sent plus received) divided by ER605 WAN bytes (both directions) over the selected range. CAVEAT: OPNsense WAN also carries traffic between the home LAN and the homelab (for example Plex to a Mac at home), so the OPNsense figure is an upper bound on the homelab's internet use, and ER605 WAN minus OPNsense WAN is NOT the rest of the household's share. Treat it as an upper bound on the homelab's share of the household total.
panels.title: Homelab share of the WAN, in range

panels.description: Source: internet_probe_* with site="home", from the internet-probe poller on rpi5, which sits behind the ER605 only. The last round's connect (tcp), reply (dns) or request (http) time per target; a target that failed in that round has no point. Measures the path from rpi5 behind the ER605, not from your devices.
panels.title: Round-trip time per target (home)

panels.description: Source: internet_probe_* with site="home", from the internet-probe poller on rpi5, which sits behind the ER605 only. TCP connect time to the ISP-facing default gateway of rpi5 (the ER605). Omitted while it is down. A rise here with a flat target RTT points at the LAN, not the ISP.
panels.title: Gateway round-trip time (home)

panels.description: Source: internet_probe_* with site="home", from the internet-probe poller on rpi5, which sits behind the ER605 only. internet_probe_failed_rounds_total / internet_probe_rounds_total, five-minute rate. A round fails only when no tcp or dns target answered. Counters restart when the poller restarts; rate() handles that.
panels.title: Failed-round ratio (home)

panels.description: Source: er605_* from the er605-poll container (roles/er605_snmp), which reads the ER605 over SNMPv3 every 30 s. Input errors (eth1 and eth0) and discards (eth1) per five minutes. Errors on the LAN side are usually a bad cable or a duplex mismatch; WAN discards are packets the router dropped on the ISP side.
panels.title: WAN and LAN errors and discards

panels.description: Source: er605_* from the er605-poll container (roles/er605_snmp), which reads the ER605 over SNMPv3 every 30 s. Age of the current PPPoE session. A drop to zero is a reconnect: the ISP ended the session or the line dropped. The sawtooth shows how often and how long each session lasted.
panels.title: PPPoE session age

panels.description: Source: er605_* from the er605-poll container (roles/er605_snmp), which reads the ER605 over SNMPv3 every 30 s. PPPoE reconnects per interval, from er605_pppoe_reconnects_total (restored from the ledger, so it survives poller restarts). A bar is a reconnect in that interval. A router reboot is not counted here; see the Outages row.
panels.title: PPPoE reconnects

panels.description: Source: er605_* from the er605-poll container (roles/er605_snmp), which reads the ER605 over SNMPv3 every 30 s. Load per core from HOST-RESOURCES hrProcessorLoad. The ER605 forwards in hardware, so these stay low even at line rate; sustained high load means a management or VPN task.
panels.title: Router CPU per core

panels.description: Source: er605_* from the er605-poll container (roles/er605_snmp), which reads the ER605 over SNMPv3 every 30 s. Physical memory by state: total, used (includes cache and buffers as the router counts them), cached and buffers. From HOST-RESOURCES hrStorage.
panels.title: Router memory

panels.description: Source: er605_* from the er605-poll container (roles/er605_snmp), which reads the ER605 over SNMPv3 every 30 s. Time since the last boot. A drop to zero is a router reboot (the poller logs router_reboot and the counters restart).
panels.title: Router uptime

panels.description: Source: er605_* from the er605-poll container (roles/er605_snmp), which reads the ER605 over SNMPv3 every 30 s. eth1 is the WAN port, eth0 the LAN side, pe-wan1_poe the PPPoE session (ifOperStatus). Red is down; gaps mean the poller or the router did not answer.
panels.title: Interface up or down

panels.description: Source: er605_* from the er605-poll container (roles/er605_snmp), which reads the ER605 over SNMPv3 every 30 s. Bytes carried by the current PPPoE session (pe-wan1_poe). Restarts from zero on a reconnect. Compare with the WAN port counters for the overhead and for traffic the session never saw.
panels.title: PPPoE session traffic

panels.description: er605_wan_up per ER605 WAN: 1 when the port is up and, for PPPoE, the session exists. Before the poller exports it (one WAN), the WAN port state er605_if_up is used.
panels.title: WAN state

panels.description: Bytes received on this WAN over the range (er605_if_octets_total joined to er605_wan_info).

targets.expr: sum by (wan) (increase(er605_if_octets_total{role="wan",direction="in"}[$__range]) * on (interface) group_left (wan) ((topk by (interface) (1, timestamp(er605_wan_info{wan=~"$wan"}))) > bool 0)) or (label_replace(sum(increase(er605_if_octets_total{role="wan",direction="in"}[$__range])), "wan", "wan1", "", "") unless on() er605_wan_info)

panels.title: Downloaded in range

panels.description: Bytes sent on this WAN over the range.

targets.expr: sum by (wan) (increase(er605_if_octets_total{role="wan",direction="out"}[$__range]) * on (interface) group_left (wan) ((topk by (interface) (1, timestamp(er605_wan_info{wan=~"$wan"}))) > bool 0)) or (label_replace(sum(increase(er605_if_octets_total{role="wan",direction="out"}[$__range])), "wan", "wan1", "", "") unless on() er605_wan_info)

panels.title: Uploaded in range

panels.description: PPPoE reconnects of this WAN over the range. Empty for a WAN that is not PPPoE.

targets.expr: round(sum((increase(er605_pppoe_reconnects_total{wan!=""}[$__range]) or label_replace(increase(er605_pppoe_reconnects_total{wan=""}[$__range]), "wan", "wan1", "", "")) and on (wan) (max by (wan) (er605_wan_info{wan=~"$wan"}) or (label_replace(vector(1), "wan", "wan1", "", "") unless on() er605_wan_info))))

panels.title: PPPoE reconnects in range

panels.description: Availability of the probe path named like this WAN (internet_probe_path_*, site home). Needs a path probe whose targets the router routes out this WAN.
panels.title: Path availability in range

panels.description: er605_wan_up per WAN, worst value in each step.

targets.expr: min by (wan) (min_over_time(er605_wan_up{wan=~"$wan"}[$__rate_interval])) or (label_replace(min(min_over_time(er605_if_up{role="wan"}[$__rate_interval])), "wan", "wan1", "", "") unless on() er605_wan_up)

panels.title: WAN up or down

panels.description: internet_probe_path_up of the path named like this WAN. Empty until a path probe is configured.
panels.title: Path up or down

panels.description: Bits per second through this WAN (er605_if_octets_total joined to er605_wan_info).

targets.expr: (sum by (wan) (rate(er605_if_octets_total{role="wan",direction="in"}[5m]) * on (interface) group_left (wan) ((topk by (interface) (1, timestamp(er605_wan_info{wan=~"$wan"}))) > bool 0)) or (label_replace(sum(rate(er605_if_octets_total{role="wan",direction="in"}[5m])), "wan", "wan1", "", "") unless on() er605_wan_info)) * 8

(sum by (wan) (rate(er605_if_octets_total{role="wan",direction="out"}[5m]) * on (interface) group_left (wan) ((topk by (interface) (1, timestamp(er605_wan_info{wan=~"$wan"}))) > bool 0)) or (label_replace(sum(rate(er605_if_octets_total{role="wan",direction="out"}[5m])), "wan", "wan1", "", "") unless on() er605_wan_info)) * 8

panels.title: Throughput

panels.description: Bytes per day through this WAN.

targets.expr: sum by (wan) (increase(er605_if_octets_total{role="wan",direction="in"}[1d]) * on (interface) group_left (wan) ((topk by (interface) (1, timestamp(er605_wan_info{wan=~"$wan"}))) > bool 0)) or (label_replace(sum(increase(er605_if_octets_total{role="wan",direction="in"}[1d])), "wan", "wan1", "", "") unless on() er605_wan_info)

sum by (wan) (increase(er605_if_octets_total{role="wan",direction="out"}[1d]) * on (interface) group_left (wan) ((topk by (interface) (1, timestamp(er605_wan_info{wan=~"$wan"}))) > bool 0)) or (label_replace(sum(increase(er605_if_octets_total{role="wan",direction="out"}[1d])), "wan", "wan1", "", "") unless on() er605_wan_info)

panels.title: Daily volume

panels.description: Age of the PPPoE session of this WAN. Empty for a WAN that is not PPPoE.

targets.expr: (er605_pppoe_session_seconds{wan!=""} or label_replace(er605_pppoe_session_seconds{wan=""}, "wan", "wan1", "", "")) and on (wan) (max by (wan) (er605_wan_info{wan=~"$wan"}) or (label_replace(vector(1), "wan", "wan1", "", "") unless on() er605_wan_info))

panels.title: PPPoE session age

panels.description: PPPoE reconnects of this WAN per step.

targets.expr: round(sum((increase(er605_pppoe_reconnects_total{wan!=""}[$__rate_interval]) or label_replace(increase(er605_pppoe_reconnects_total{wan=""}[$__rate_interval]), "wan", "wan1", "", "")) and on (wan) (max by (wan) (er605_wan_info{wan=~"$wan"}) or (label_replace(vector(1), "wan", "wan1", "", "") unless on() er605_wan_info))))

panels.title: PPPoE reconnects

panels.description: Round-trip time of the targets of the path named like this WAN. Empty until a path probe is configured.
panels.title: Path round-trip time

panels.description: Failed probes per minute on the path named like this WAN, per target.
panels.title: Path failures per minute

panels.description: Source: the internet-probe journal lines in Loki (30 days), one per closed outage, from rpi5 (site home, behind the ER605). Fields are the labels that `| logfmt` extracts from the line. closed_by=restart means the poller restarted during the outage. Open outages appear only in the logs panel below. Older: internet-probe.py --report outages on rpi5.
panels.title: Internet outages (home)

panels.description: Source: the er605-poll container's pppoe_reconnect lines in Loki (30 days; container logs are shipped by Alloy with the labels job=docker, container=er605-poll, host=ubuntu-dev). at is when the new PPPoE session started, previous_session_seconds how long the one before it lasted. Older: --report reconnects on ubuntu-dev.
panels.title: PPPoE reconnects

panels.description: Source: the internet-probe journal lines in Loki (30 days) from rpi5: outage_start (a confirmed outage began), outage_end, and blip (fewer than 2 failed rounds, no ledger entry). One line per event, no per-round noise.
panels.title: Outage events and blips (home)

panels.description: Source: the er605-poll container's journal lines in Loki (30 days): pppoe_reconnect, router_reboot (at is the estimated boot time) and poll_error (rate-limited to one per 10 minutes). Container logs reach Loki through Alloy's Docker source: labels job=docker, container=er605-poll, compose_service=er605-poll, host=ubuntu-dev.
panels.title: Router events

panels.description: Source: the poller's hourly `usage` lines in Loki (30 days); set the time picker up to 30 days. WAN eth1 bytes, whole household. Compare with the Prometheus figure in Overview (7 days). Older: --report month on ubuntu-dev.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time({host="ubuntu-dev", job="docker", container="er605-poll"} |~ "^usage " | logfmt | unwrap download_bytes [$__range]))

panels.title: Downloaded in range (ledger)

panels.description: Source: the poller's hourly `usage` lines in Loki (30 days); set the time picker up to 30 days. WAN eth1 bytes, whole household.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time({host="ubuntu-dev", job="docker", container="er605-poll"} |~ "^usage " | logfmt | unwrap upload_bytes [$__range]))

panels.title: Uploaded in range (ledger)

panels.description: Source: the poller's `usage` lines in Loki (30 days), one per closed UTC hour. A bar is drawn when its line was written, which is when the hour closed, so it sits up to an hour after the traffic. Older: --report hour on ubuntu-dev.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time({host="ubuntu-dev", job="docker", container="er605-poll"} |~ "^usage " | logfmt | unwrap download_bytes [1h]))
sum(sum_over_time({host="ubuntu-dev", job="docker", container="er605-poll"} |~ "^usage " | logfmt | unwrap upload_bytes [1h]))

panels.title: Hourly volume (ledger)

panels.description: Source: the usage lines the poller writes once per closed hour: hour (UTC), download_bytes and upload_bytes from the WAN port. The ledger itself is usage.db on ubuntu-dev (--report hour|day|month).
panels.title: Usage lines (ledger)

panels.description: Bytes per ER605 WAN; the total rows sum all WANs. Source: PostgreSQL net_history (datasource Network history), rolled up hourly by net-history and kept forever; always the last 24 months, whatever the time picker says.

targets.rawSql: SELECT month::timestamp AS time, wan || ' download' AS metric, download_bytes AS value FROM net.monthly_wan WHERE month >= (date_trunc('month', now() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') - interval '23 months')::date AND wan <> 'total' UNION ALL SELECT month::timestamp, wan || ' upload', upload_bytes FROM net.monthly_wan WHERE month >= (date_trunc('month', now() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') - interval '23 months')::date AND wan <> 'total' ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Download and upload per month, per WAN

panels.description: Reconnects per ER605 WAN. Source: PostgreSQL net_history (datasource Network history), rolled up hourly by net-history and kept forever; always the last 24 months, whatever the time picker says.

targets.rawSql: SELECT month::timestamp AS time, wan AS metric, pppoe_reconnects AS value FROM net.monthly_wan WHERE month >= (date_trunc('month', now() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') - interval '23 months')::date AND wan <> 'total' ORDER BY 1

panels.title: PPPoE reconnects per month

panels.description: Whole-site availability of the home internet (probe on rpi5). Source: PostgreSQL net_history (datasource Network history), rolled up hourly by net-history and kept forever; always the last 24 months, whatever the time picker says.

targets.rawSql: SELECT month::timestamp AS time, site AS metric, availability AS value FROM net.monthly_internet WHERE month >= (date_trunc('month', now() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') - interval '23 months')::date AND site = 'home' ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Home internet availability per month

panels.description: Availability of each per-WAN probe path (internet_probe_path_*). Empty until path probes exist. Source: PostgreSQL net_history (datasource Network history), rolled up hourly by net-history and kept forever; always the last 24 months, whatever the time picker says.

targets.rawSql: SELECT month::timestamp AS time, name AS metric, availability AS value FROM net.monthly_path WHERE month >= (date_trunc('month', now() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') - interval '23 months')::date AND site = 'home' ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Path availability per month, per WAN

panels.description: Last 12 months; wan = total is the household. Source: PostgreSQL net_history (datasource Network history), kept forever.

targets.rawSql: SELECT to_char(month, 'YYYY-MM') AS month, wan, days, download_bytes, upload_bytes, total_bytes, pppoe_reconnects, partial_days FROM net.monthly_wan WHERE month >= (date_trunc('month', now() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') - interval '11 months')::date ORDER BY month DESC, (wan = 'total') DESC, wan

panels.title: Monthly volume per WAN

panels.description: Closed home internet, per-WAN path and ER605 WAN outages, newest first (last 500). Source: PostgreSQL net_history (datasource Network history), kept forever.

targets.rawSql: SELECT started_at AS "Start", ended_at AS "End", site AS "Site", kind AS "Kind", name AS "Name", target AS "Target", duration_seconds AS duration_seconds, cause AS "Cause", closed_by AS "Closed by" FROM net.outage_events WHERE kind IN ('internet', 'path', 'wan') AND site = 'home' ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 500

panels.title: Outage history, home (permanent)

list.definition: query_result(max by (wan) (er605_wan_info) or (label_replace(vector(1), "wan", "wan1", "", "") unless on() er605_wan_info))
list.name: wan
list.label: WAN

query.query: query_result(max by (wan) (er605_wan_info) or (label_replace(vector(1), "wan", "wan1", "", "") unless on() er605_wan_info))

title: Home ISP
